title: Why are credit card rates so high? What are the economics of credit card banking?
discussion_signal: The NBER announcement makes the consumer-finance scale visible: the paper uses account-level data covering 550 million monthly accounts to ask why credit-card rates and lending economics are unusually high. The public signal points toward a household-use and lender-return tension, while leaving borrower-level welfare open.
linked_research_question: How do broad household use, credit-card rates, default risk, issuer returns, rewards, and repayment burdens combine into consumer welfare or market-power outcomes?
limits: The announcement does not provide a household panel or borrower-level repayment burden
Account coverage is not the same as household welfare or product choice
A high rate or return does not by itself prove excessive pricing or consumer harm
